meta.description: Custom C++ and OpenGL engine created to power Kobold Delvers and real-time cellular-automata gameplay.

content.title: Sand Forge Engine
about: Sand Forge Engine is the custom engine developed to power Kobold Delvers. It was built in C++ and OpenGL with the goal of supporting a real-time cellular-automata world, fast rendering, and a lightweight gameplay layer tailored to the needs of the project.
The engine acts as the technical base of the game: it manages the simulation, rendering, input, UI, audio, entities, and the transformations between screen, world, chunk, and cell coordinates.

A major part of the work focused on keeping the simulation and rendering efficient. The world is treated as a grid of cells, but only the necessary regions are updated or uploaded to the GPU when possible, reducing unnecessary work and making the system more scalable.
features: Real-time cellular-automata simulation designed for interactive materials
Custom OpenGL renderer for drawing the cell world and game entities
Partial GPU texture updates to avoid resending the full world every frame
Coordinate conversion layer between screen, world, chunks, and cells
Entity system used for gameplay objects such as kobolds, player tools, hazards, and interactable elements
Input layer for keyboard, mouse, camera movement, and gameplay actions
UI system used for menus, level flow, controls, credits, sandbox tools, and player feedback
Audio system based on miniaudio for music and sound effects
CMake-based project structure prepared for development builds and Steam distribution
learnings: Building a specialized engine around the constraints of a single game idea
Structuring a simulation-heavy project so the world, renderer, entities, and UI remain separated but connected
Improving performance by avoiding unnecessary full-world GPU uploads
Designing coordinate transformations robust enough for editing, simulation, rendering, and player interaction
Understanding the trade-off between engine flexibility and the simplicity needed to finish a complete game
